artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol. Consider the multinomial coefficient $\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}=\frac{(4k)!}{(k!)^4}$ and the Bernoulli polynomial $B_{n}(x)$.

Prove or disprove the following statements.

(1) If $\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right)=1$ (equivalently $p\equiv 1,3\pmod 8$) and $p=x^{2}+2y^{2}$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$, then
$$\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^{3}}{(-64)^{k}}\;\equiv\;\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}}{28^{4k}}\;\equiv\;4x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

(2) If $\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right)=-1$ (equivalently $p\equiv 5,7\pmod 8$), then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^{3}}{(-64)^{k}}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}},$$
and, provided $p\neq 7$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}}{28^{4k}}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

(3) For every positive integer $a$ and every odd prime $p\notin\{3,7\}$,
$$p^{a}\sum_{k=0}^{p^{a}-1}\frac{40k+3}{28^{4k}}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\;\equiv\;3\!\left(\frac{p^{a}-(p^{a-1})}{?}\right)\;-\;\frac{5p^{2}}{392}\,B_{p-2}(1)\pmod{p^{3}}$$
(where the right-hand side is to be interpreted as in the standard formulation: $3(p^{a})-(p^{a-1})\cdot\frac{5p^{2}}{392}B_{p-2}(1)$ modulo $p^{3}$, with $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ extended multiplicatively).

(4) The numbers
$$a_{n}\;:=\;\frac{1}{2n(2n+1)}\binom{2n}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(40k+3)\,\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\,28^{4(n-1-k)}$$
are integers for all $n=2,3,4,\dots$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not yield a definitive proof or disproof of this specific multi-part conjecture (Sun's Conjecture A28) involving the sums $\sum\binom{2k}{k}^3/(-64)^k$ and $\sum\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}/28^{4k}$ together with the representation $p=x^2+2y^2$. Related Sun supercongruences (e.g. $\sum (4k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3/64^k\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2r}}$) have been proven, but the precise statements (1)–(4) above do not appear to be fully resolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Proof of a supercongruence modulo p^{2r} (Guo)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves a related Sun supercongruence involving (2k choose k)^3 / 64^k modulo p^{2r}.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct Sun supercongruences have been proven; not the specific A28 statements.

status_evidence.title: Proof of a recent conjecture of Z.-W. Sun (arXiv:1604.05019)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves one of Sun's congruence conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing work on Sun's many congruence conjectures, with specific A28 not identified as resolved.
